title: Start the blocking input

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that a small task that releases a big dependent task should go first, because every minute it waits delays the big task too

misconception: Do the quick, satisfying tasks first; the small input task can wait.
objective: Identify the work that releases a blocked successor.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: A 2-minute input unlocks a 30-minute build. A 2-minute input unlocks a 30-minute build. Polish (10 min) first or input first: when does the build finish? Correct option: 10 minutes later with polish first. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Reset to unverified by demo-builder 2026-10-15 (r11 fix plan W9): hook, question or options replaced by the W9 prediction line (options reordered for TP-8). Not checked by the builder. | FC pass 52 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, W-1144/W2): DISPUTED. The keyed answer is true only for one reading of 'input first'. Question: 'Polish (10 min) first or input first: when does the build finish?' Key: '10 minutes later with polish first'. On this stage, 'Swap first' turns polish→input→build into input→polish→build, which is input first, and the build is still done at minute 42, the same as polish first (own run of queueResult; the 'Build done' chip shows 42 both times). Only input→build→polish ('Try target') gives 32. A learner who swaps sees the distractor 'Same either way' come true. Fix (demo-builder, claim text and studyCatalog together): ask about the order that is meant, e.g. 'Polish (10 min) first, or input and then the build: when does the build finish?', or make 'Swap first' not produce input→polish→build. Re-check after the change.

claims.text: The build depends on the input. Doing unrelated work first delays release, even when that unrelated work is useful.

Read StudyLesson.tsx (order stage) and queueObservation in src/lib/lifehacks/studyStages.ts first; own run of queueResult/queueObservation (scratchpad fc52/sim.mts): polish→input→build: build done at 42, waiting 22; input→polish→build (Swap first): build still 42, waiting 14; input→build→polish (Try target): build 32, waiting 34, reveal adds '12 more minutes of waiting ... the goal here is build done sooner (minute 32, not 42)'. claims.text: Stage: input 2 min; build 30 min, needs the input; polish 10 min. Polish first: build done at minute 42. Input first, then build: build done at minute 32, 10 minutes sooner, while total waiting rises from 22 to 34 minutes.

recall.question: A colleague's 2-hour build cannot start until you send a 5-minute config. You also have 30 minutes of tidying. What first?
recall.why: The short input releases the dependent build; doing the tidying first delays the build by 30 minutes.
